messages:
Ravi: Customer on-prem sees intermittent streaming cutouts when responses run >30s. Two example request IDs from their logs: req-0a1b2c3d and req-9f8e7d6c. They sit behind a corporate proxy and use signed cookies for auth. Can someone help produce a minimal cURL smoke repro we can send them?

Emily: Sure — let's get a minimal reproducible curl that preserves streaming and includes headers. Ask the customer to run the exact command (replace REDACTED values) and paste the full output (including response headers). Example I usually send: 

```bash
curl -v -N --http1.1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Cookie: sf_signed=REDACTED_COOKIE" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: test-req-1234" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=jumbo-lite'
```

Emily: Notes: -v for headers, -N/--no-buffer to stream directly, --http1.1 because some proxies downgrade http2 and break SSE. If they have a corporate proxy, ask them to run the same with `--proxy <proxy>` or set env vars so we reproduce the same path.

Sam: Also ask them to run a trace file so we can see the wire-level exchange: 
```bash
curl -v -N --http1.1 --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace.txt \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Cookie: sf_signed=REDACTED_COOKIE" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=jumbo-lite'
```
That trace will capture TLS handshake, request/response headers and any resets.

Support Bot: Quick checklist for the bundle we need to correlate with our side: 
- curl-trace.txt from the run (trace-ascii)
- stdout from curl (so we can confirm chunk boundaries)
- the service-side logs for the request IDs (req-0a1b2c3d, req-9f8e7d6c)
- proxy logs (if accessible) and timestamp range (first_message_ts .. last_message_ts)
- tcpdump or pcap for ~60s around repro (optional but very helpful)

Ravi: Good. Customer also reports a 502/connection reset visible in client. Should we ask them to confirm response headers include `transfer-encoding: chunked` and not `content-length`?

Emily: Yes. Ask them to run a quick header-only check too: 
```bash
curl -I -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Cookie: sf_signed=REDACTED_COOKIE" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=jumbo-lite'
```
and paste the headers. We want to see: Server, Transfer-Encoding, Connection, any proxy-added headers (Via, X-Forwarded-*), and our response trace id header (x-rw-request-id).

Sam: Also ask them to append `-H "X-Debug-Mode: true"` for a short run so we can trigger slightly more verbose logs on our end if they consent. And include `--max-time 300` to avoid short client timeouts during long responses.

Ravi: I'll send the commands to the customer. If they run the trace and we get a truncated stream, what should we look for on our side?

Emily: Look for these patterns: 
- upstream service emitted the final event then connection tear (200 + normal EOF) vs proxy reset mid-chunk (RST/TCP FIN without final event)
- mismatched content-encoding/transfer-encoding inserted by proxy
- TLS renegotiation or client idle timeout from proxy
- our logs: check for an explicit shutdown from the runtime for that req-id and the exact timestamp in ms.

Support Bot: If they can't share pcap, a small tcpdump of SYN/FIN/RST events filtered to the request IP and port is acceptable: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/repro.pcap host <customer-ip> and port 443 and '(tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-rst|tcp-fin) != 0)'`

Ravi: Perfect — I'll ask them to run the three commands (streaming curl, trace-ascii, header-only) and attach the files. I'll also request the proxy logs and confirm whether they have any inline WAF that may cut long-lived chunked responses.

Emily: One more tip for reproducibility: include a deterministic prompt that triggers >30s generation so we get the long tail (paste the prompt text). If they can reproduce locally without the proxy, that narrows things quickly.

Sam: If they come back with the traces, ping me and I'll correlate req-0a1b2c3d against our logs and check for any middleware aborts. :thumbsup:

Ravi: Thanks everyone — sending the repro checklist now to the customer.
